Content: Small update about the eFuse. I've tested two more chips with eFuse from the Run 1. All Wishbone and async eFuse blocks at 5V worked flawlesly. WB blocks also passed 5 million reads endurance test without a single failed bit. This makes 3 successfuly tested eFuse chips in total. Not much, but I assume this means that WB & async eFuse blocks are safe to use in 5V designs 🙂.  Now for the downside, current SPI efuse wrapper contains an error which might lead to hold violations and SPI interface not functioning properly in some cases. So **please do not use the current SPI eFuse IP**. I'm planing to release a revised SPI wrapper in a couple of weeks, together with the 3.3V compatible eFuse IP with a separate 5V supply for writing.

Author: tholin
Content:
I have a sad update. My attempt to build the first self-compiling integrated circuit has most likely failed.
The goal was it to make a custom RTL-to-GDSII flow tool (FeatherLane) with a focus on being lightweight, use it on RTL for a RISC-V core, tape it out, and have the chip run FeatherLane on its own RTL, re-producing its own layout.
However, today I found a one-line bug in FeatherLane’s router that accesses a single byte out of the bounds of a malloc’d array. It only uses it to decide on a continue, and if it accidentally continues when its not supposed to, the only effect is a slightly uglier looking route. Its still DRC correct and electrically correct (LVS passes), but means the resulting layout is not exactly 1:1 with what I taped out. Unless I can reproduce the exact state my whole computer was in on the day I ran FeatherLane on the RTL for tapeout. The read is non-deterministic, so whether it continues or not is random. This loop is executed thousands of times.

Author: tholin
Content: So unless I get to tape out a chip just dedicated to FeatherLane generated layouts (unlikely, considering my finances and the fact that such a chip would not be useful outside of making this accomplishment), I’ll have to accept second-best.

Author: tholin
Content: This took over half a year to pull off, and now its ruined by a single bad line of code.
